subject: Dedicated transition — proposed conversion-credit taper & SLA bucket model
messages:
From: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial ask on credits and SLAs

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for walking us through Redwood Dedicated yesterday. Procurement asked for a clearer picture of how you intend to transition us off hosted spend — specifically:

- How conversion credits will amortize across the commit term (we currently spend about $85k/mo hosted)
- Whether bridge months are available if the Dedicated pool isn't fully online by August 1
- How throughput guarantees map to the GPU pool sizing (we have seasonal spikes up to 120 concurrent heavy generation workers)

Could you share a simple taper schedule and a proposed SLA bucket model so we can baseline with legal? Also copying Evan (infra) for sizing questions.

Best,
Ava

--
Ava Reynolds
Director, Platform Operations | Nimbus Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial ask on credits and SLAs

Ava — thanks, and great questions. Quick summary to start:

- Conversion credits: we offer a time-phased credit that offsets hosted ARR against initial Dedicated commits. Typical structure: 50% credit applied in month 1 of the commit, then a 25% taper in months 2–3, and final 25% as a rolling offset across months 4–12. We can customize the split for larger deals.
- Bridge months: we can provide up to 2 bridge months of token-level billing at hosted rates while your Dedicated pool warms up; that can be converted into credits if you hit the committed throughput targets.
- SLA buckets: instead of one monolithic latency SLO, we propose three buckets (baseline, burst, and sustained). Each bucket maps to reserved vGPU slabs and a throughput floor; this gives predictable pricing for baseline traffic while preserving cost controls during bursts.

I'm attaching a short proposal and an example SLA-Buckets workbook to show how pool sizing maps to expected p95 token latency and tokens/sec. Neha — can you confirm the flexible taper options we can offer for RID-98721? Aisha/Karthik — assume Nimbus needs sizing validation for 120 concurrent heavy gen workers (sequence lengths ~1.5k tokens).

I'll follow up with a worked example by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial ask on credits and SLAs

Marcus — notes on flexibility for this tier (internal):

- For deals > $750k ARR equivalent we can shift from the standard 50/25/25 to 60/20/20 or front-load credits (70/15/15) if the customer needs greater near-term relief; need finance approval for >70%.
- Bridge months: 2 months standard, can extend to 3 with repayment schedule tied to utilization milestones (70% of committed throughput reached).
- SLA buckets: pricing impact roughly +8–12% for adding a dedicated burst slab that guarantees <120ms p95 at 2x baseline throughput.

Action: I will draft two alternative credit schedules (conservative + customer-friendly) and mark the finance escalation path if Nimbus requests >70% front-loaded credits.

— Neha
Head of Enterprise Sales Operations
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evan Holt <evan.holt@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated transition — proposed conversion-credit taper & SLA bucket model

Hi Ava — attaching the worked examples I promised. TL;DR of the attachment:

- Example A (conservative): 50/25/25 credit split; 2 bridge months; baseline slab sized for 90 concurrent heavy workers, burst slab covers up to 140 workers at defined uplift pricing.
- Example B (accelerated): 60/20/20 credit split; 3rd bridge month contingent on hitting 70% utilization by month 2; includes an optional on-call capacity buffer for scheduled seasonal peaks.

Evan — for your sizing review: Example A baseline uses an 8-GPU vPool (A100xlarge equivalent) with continuous batching targets of 65 tokens/sec per GPU and KV cache hit assumptions (~30% reuse). If Nimbus' workload has higher KV reuse, you could reduce baseline GPUs by 1–2.

Next steps: can we set a 30-minute call tomorrow to pick A vs B and confirm bridge timing? If Nimbus signs by June 10 we can lock preferred pricing and schedule a July ramp.

Attachments: RID-98721-DedicatedProposal_v2.pdf; SLA-Buckets_v1.xlsx

Regards,
Marcus
From: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Holt <evan.holt@nimbushealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T10:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated transition — proposed conversion-credit taper & SLA bucket model

Thanks Marcus — helpful. A couple of clarifying Qs before we schedule finance/legal review:

1) For the bridge months: if we consume them and then fall short of utilization milestones, is there an overage reconciliation or repayment?
2) Is the burst slab billed as a flat monthly overprovision (we pay for reserved burst GPUs) or on actual burst usage?

Also, procurement prefers credits to be applied as a dollar offset on the invoice rather than as a separate line item; any issues with that?

Ava

Ava — quick answers and proposed legal-friendly language for procurement: 

1) Bridge month reconciliation: if bridge months are used but utilization milestones are not met by the end of the agreed measurement window, the bridge usage converts to billed hosted usage (no retroactive cash repayment). If customer requests credit conversion despite missed milestones, we require a repayment schedule spread across the remaining commit months (example clause in attached proposal).

2) Burst slab billing: two options — reserved-burst (flat monthly fee for reserved burst GPUs) or on-demand-burst (billed per actual oversubscription tokens/sec above baseline with a discounted rate). Our standard is reserved-burst for predictability; on-demand is available when customers prefer pay-for-use.

3) Invoice treatment: no problem — finance prefers credits as invoice offsets. We will provide both an accounting-friendly credit memo and a line item description that legal can reference.

Suggested next steps:
- Marcus/Neha: finalize the favored credit split (A or B) and mark whether procurement prefers reserved vs on-demand burst.
- Nimbus: confirm whether you want the 3rd bridge month contingent (Example B) or stick with 2 months (Example A).
- Schedule 30-min sync (I propose Thursday 10am PT).

If that sounds good I'll loop legal and send an updated term sheet for signature.

Best,
Marcus
